subject.title: Feature request: cron job auto-retry on failure (--retry-count, --retry-delay)

question: Should OpenClaw add per-job cron retry options and persisted retry policy, or keep retry behavior as the existing global transient scheduler policy?
rationale: Current main already fixed the broad recurring transient retry gap, but the remaining request defines new public CLI, Gateway, and stored job semantics that automation should not choose without maintainer product/API intent.

options.title: Review per-job retry API
options.body: Use the linked implementation candidate and this issue to decide exact flag names, persisted fields, defaults, and upgrade proof before landing.

options.title: Keep global retry only
options.body: Close the feature direction after explicitly deciding the existing global transient retry/backoff behavior is enough and per-job policy should not be added now.

options.title: Fold into reason-aware guardrails
options.body: Route the remaining policy work into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/14376 if retry controls should be tied to failure classification, circuit breakers, and observability.

recommendation.title: Review per-job retry API
recommendation.body: Use the linked implementation candidate and this issue to decide exact flag names, persisted fields, defaults, and upgrade proof before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete most recently merged the recurring cron retry behavior that the remaining per-job contract would extend.
